title: Weights & Measures — Real Pixels, Real Seconds
description: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report — Bai et al. (Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, 2025); with Qwen2-VL — Wang et al. (Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, 2024) and Qwen3-VL Technical Report — Bai et al. (Qwen Team, 2025)
show_notes:
Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report — Bai et al. (Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, 2025); with Qwen2-VL — Wang et al. (Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, 2024) and Qwen3-VL Technical Report — Bai et al. (Qwen Team, 2025)

How does a language model see? Jack and Molly take apart Alibaba's open-weight Qwen2.5-VL: an image is cut into 14-pixel patches and merged so that each token covers a 28-by-28-pixel square, a picture makes as many tokens as its size needs, within a default budget of 4 to 16,384 per image (native resolution, from its predecessor Qwen2-VL, which credits Google DeepMind's NaViT), and every token carries a three-part position stamp for time, row and column. The report's own additions are window attention in an encoder the team trained itself, a time stamp tied to real seconds rather than frame counts, and boxes and points written in pixel coordinates. On the ScreenSpot Pro test, which asks a model to point at a named element on a screenshot, the 72B model went from its predecessor's 1.6 percent to 43.6, while it led on most document tests, including DocVQA and OCRBench, trailed Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Aguvis-72B on the live-computer OSWorld test, and did not lead on standard box-grounding tests. Then the twist: in November 2025 the Qwen3-VL report went back to a 0-to-1,000 coordinate scale, wrote time as text, and swapped the home-grown encoder for Google's SigLIP 2, while the 2.5 weights became a common starting point for other models. The policy thread: the Ninth Circuit's August 2026 Amazon v. Perplexity decision on a screenshot-reading browser assistant that shops on Amazon, and proposed Federal Rule of Evidence 707 on machine-generated evidence, set beside document readers that can write text that isn't on the page.

Notes: Qwen2.5-VL's benchmark scores are the Qwen team's own runs, without error bars (the report does not say which rival scores it ran and which it copied), and the report never switches off its own design choices to test them, so no one can say which choice bought which gain. Its prose claims more than its tables show: it calls its OSWorld result comparable, though it scored 8.83 to Claude 3.5 Sonnet's 14.90 and Aguvis-72B's 10.26, and on standard box-grounding tests InternVL2.5 scores above it on all eight splits. The comparison with Qwen2-VL's grounding scores crosses two reports that may use different evaluation settings. Qwen3-VL's reasons for its changes are its stated reasons; none was tested against the Qwen2.5-VL design. Hugging Face download counts are file requests, not users. In vacating a preliminary injunction, the Ninth Circuit held that, under the federal anti-hacking statute and California's version and on this record, the user did the accessing; it left tort claims open, said Amazon can still regulate access through its terms of service, and sent the case back to the district court. Proposed Rule 707 would apply the expert-testimony standard to machine output offered without an expert only where that output would be subject to that standard if a witness gave it, and it exempts simple scientific instruments; as of the rules committee's September 2026 report it is under continued consideration, not law.

Jack and Molly are AI-generated hosts; research and script by Oggy.
